messages:
jamie: FYI: since 09:10 UTC we're seeing intermittent DNS timeouts from GPU-serving pods in eu-central-1. ~12-18% of inference requests fail with "Name or service not known". Not all nodes, seems bursty.

sana: Are failures correlated with pod restarts / cold starts or a specific node pool?

jamie: Mostly on the new GPU pool (g4dn-like) after the autoscaler added nodes. No pod restarts observed. Latency spikes then NX.

infra-bot: incident #INC-6712 created (severity: high) — assigned to eng-infra oncall.

oncall: Picking this up. Any obvious DNS errors on the kube nodes / node-local-dns pods?

jamie: Pasted a couple of quick dumps from one affected node:

--- /etc/resolv.conf ---
# Generated by node-resolver
search eu-central.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
nameserver 169.254.20.10  # node-local-dns
nameserver 127.0.0.53     # systemd-resolved fallback
options ndots:5 timeout:2 rotate\n--- end ---

jamie: dig against node-local-dns shows timeouts during the window:

$ dig @169.254.20.10 model-registry.internal +short +time=2; (no reply)
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached

sana: Can you paste the node-local-dns logs around a failure? Also any nf_conntrack messages in dmesg?

jamie: node-local-dns logs have repeated "upstream query dropped: rate limit" messages and SERVFAIL spikes. Kernel dmesg on the node shows:

[ 12345.678901] nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
[ 12345.679012] nf_conntrack: falling back to least recently used entry

sasha: That suggests SNAT/conntrack exhaustion. GPU nodes have many pods doing short lived external DNS queries when pulling model manifests; cold-starts = query burst.

tim: Two hypotheses: 1) node-local-cache is forwarding too many concurrent queries to cloud DNS and hitting GCP/AWS DNS QPS/rate limits; 2) conntrack table too small for bursty NAT from many pods + ephemeral ports exhausted. Either can produce timeouts.

sana: Quick mitigation options?

sasha: Short term: bump nf_conntrack_max via sysctl on affected nodes and restart kube-proxy to reset conntrack allocations. Also enable conntrack hashsize increase.

jamie: Confirmed bumping net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max from 262144 -> 1000000 reduced dmesg noise on that node. After that, error rate dropped from ~15% to ~1% for a few minutes.

oncall: Was that safe to do cluster-wide? Any memory impact?

sasha: We measured ~2-3MB extra mem per 100k entries; still fine on 64GB GPU nodes. We'll roll to the whole pool as emergency patch.

tim: Medium-term: add per-node DNS throttling/backoff in node-local-dns and enable query coalescing (collapse identical outstanding queries). Also tune upstream health checks to avoid immediate failover under short bursts.

sana: Also recommend increasing node-local-dns cache TTL for registry/model hostnames (they change rarely) to reduce churn. Right now TTLs are low because service returns short TTLs for sharded registry endpoints. Can we pin model-registry to internal ELB IPs for cold-start path?

jamie: We tried pinning one model host to internal NLB and cold-start failures stopped for that model. So upstream rate limiting + caching behavior is the likely root.

infra-bot: Deployment notice: rolling restart of kube-proxy scheduled to 2026-03-18T10:05Z (emergency).

sasha: Long-term: 1) make model fetch resilient to DNS churn (client-side retry with jitter + local hostcache), 2) bake more models into images for the hottest artifacts, 3) add a lightweight per-node forwarder that does request coalescing and QPS shaping before hitting cloud resolver.

jamie: Agreed. Also adding a telemetry counter to count "upstream rate-limited responses" from node-local-dns so we can threshold-alert before user-visible errors.

tim: Action items:
- sana: roll sysctl bump + kube-proxy restart to affected pool (done, monitor)
- sasha: patch node-local-dns for coalescing + TTL overrides (PR in progress)
- jamie: add telemetry alert for upstream rate-limit spikes
- infra: investigate if cloud DNS QPS quota needs bump / use local resolver cluster behind private IP.

jamie: Current status: error rate back down to baseline after conntrack bump + kube-proxy restart, but we'll keep the incident open until node-local-dns PR and telemetry are merged.

oncall: Thanks all — please post updates here. :thumbsup:
